title: How does a 4-level x86-64 page walk turn a virtual address into a physical one?

glossary.note: A small cache of finished address translations.
Holds the physical base of the top page table.
The last-level entry that names a frame.

key_points: A page walk is four dependent table lookups, each indexed by 9 bits of the address.
CR3 holds the top table; each entry names the next table, and the last names the frame.
TLBs and huge pages exist to avoid the full walk.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mo delivers parcels to a building with four directories, one per floor. Each parcel label holds five numbers.

beats.speaker: mo
beats.text: So four numbers pick rows on four floors?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: That's the trick your CPU uses. A virtual address is 48 bits: four nine-bit indexes, then a twelve-bit offset.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The CR3 register holds the physical address of the top directory. Index times eight picks the entry.
beats.say: The C R three register holds the physical address of the top directory. Index times eight picks the entry.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: That entry's address bits name the next directory. Repeat: pud, pmd, pte.
beats.say: That entry's address bits name the next directory. Repeat: P U D, P M D, P T E.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The last entry names the frame. Add the offset, and you're at the byte.

beats.speaker: mo
beats.text: Four lookups, to read one byte?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Here the analogy stops. Floors cost nothing to visit, but these directories live in RAM. A TLB miss means four dependent memory reads.
beats.say: Here the analogy stops. Floors cost nothing to visit, but these directories live in RAM. A T L B miss means four dependent memory reads.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Each waits for the one before. So the CPU caches finished translations in the TLB, and a huge page stops the walk early.
beats.say: Each waits for the one before. So the CPU caches finished translations in the T L B, and a huge page stops the walk early.

beats.speaker: mo
beats.text: What does Linux call these floors?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: pgd, p4d, pud, pmd, pte. With four levels, the p4d level is folded away.
beats.say: P G D, P four D, P U D, P M D, P T E. With four levels, the P four D level is folded away.
